summary: The normalized exponential distribution on a cylindrical (vr, vx) velocity mesh before any moment compensation: one temperature per axial shift, the molecule-count factor in the exponent, a -80 tail floor that preserves the analytic peak, and normalization by the caller-supplied cylindrical cell volumes. Composes with the cylindrical velocity quadrature and stops before any moment-compensation step.

capability: The normalized exponential distribution on a cylindrical (vr, vx) velocity mesh before any moment compensation: one temperature per axial shift, the molecule-count factor in the exponent, a -80 tail floor that preserves the analytic peak, and normalization by the caller-supplied cylindrical cell volumes. Composes with the cylindrical velocity quadrature and stops before any moment-compensation step.
operation: vr, vx, normalization temperature, axial shifts in m/s, per-shift temperatures, mass, molecule count and cell volumes -> per-shift normalized distribution, thermal speed and raw exponent
discovery.model: discretized shifted Maxwellian exponential seed on an explicit mesh; any downstream moment-compensation step is deliberately outside this leaf
discovery.geometry: velocity space, cylindrical: radial speed vr and axial velocity vx; the axial shift is applied to the vx axis
discovery.boundary: argument == 0 keeps exp(0) = 1 before normalization; exponents at or below -80 keep the exp(-80) tail floor; the distribution is never exactly zero; molecule_count must be exactly 1 or 2; every accepted call returns finite distributions

identity.relation: the normalized exponential seed of the shifted-Maxwellian relation on a cylindrical velocity mesh, before moment compensation
identity.direction: vr, vx, normalization temperature, axial shifts in m/s, per-shift temperatures, mass, molecule count and cell volumes -> per-shift normalized distribution, thermal speed and raw exponent
identity.definition: With m_H = 1.6726231e-27 kg (the hydrogen mass constant), vth = sqrt(2 e T_norm / (m m_H)). The raw exponent is -(vr^2 + (vx - shift/vth)^2) * molecule_count * T_norm / T_shift per shift. The raw seed is exp(argument) where -80 < argument <= 0 and exp(-80) otherwise. In particular, a node exactly at the shifted peak keeps exp(0) = 1, as required by the Maxwell-Boltzmann definition f=C exp[-mass*|v-U|^2/(2 e T)]; the returned exponent reports the raw value even in the floored tail. The distribution is normalized per shift by the supplied cell volumes: sum(volume * distribution) = 1 per shift.
identity.model: discretized shifted Maxwellian exponential seed on an explicit mesh; any downstream moment-compensation step is deliberately outside this leaf
identity.geometry: velocity space, cylindrical: radial speed vr and axial velocity vx; the axial shift is applied to the vx axis
identity.coordinates: vr and vx in the caller's normalized velocity unit; shifts in m/s are divided by the thermal speed into mesh units
identity.boundary: argument == 0 keeps exp(0) = 1 before normalization; exponents at or below -80 keep the exp(-80) tail floor; the distribution is never exactly zero; molecule_count must be exactly 1 or 2; every accepted call returns finite distributions
assumptions: The cell volumes are the caller's; the cylindrical velocity quadrature produces exactly the measure this normalization consumes.
The seed is the pre-compensation stage: a caller that needs a moment-compensated distribution must not treat this seed as final.

AMU_KG = 1.6726231e-27 kg is the hydrogen mass constant, not the standard atomic mass unit; the historical name is kept for compatibility. ELEMENTARY_CHARGE_C = 1.602177e-19 C is frozen at the same historical value. Neither constant is a current CODATA estimate.
molecule_count is a convention of this relation: the exponent carries a factor 2 for molecular hydrogen relative to atomic hydrogen.

inputs.name: vx
inputs.description: Normalized axial-velocity mesh; the shift is applied to this axis.

inputs.name: tnorm_ev
inputs.description: Normalization temperature fixing the thermal speed that converts shifts into mesh units.

inputs.name: shifted_vx_m_s
inputs.description: Axial shifts of the Maxwellian peaks, one per layer.

inputs.name: temperature_ev
inputs.description: Per-shift temperatures, same length as the shifts.
inputs.constraints: A finite one-dimensional array with strictly positive entries and the shifts' shape.

inputs.name: mass_amu
inputs.description: Species mass factor relative to the hydrogen mass constant (1.6726231e-27 kg), despite the historical parameter name; fixes the thermal speed.

inputs.name: molecule_count
inputs.description: Molecule-count factor of the exponent: 1 for atomic, 2 for molecular hydrogen.

inputs.name: cylindrical_volume
inputs.description: Cell volumes of the cylindrical velocity mesh, rows matched to vr and columns to vx.

outputs.name: distribution
outputs.description: The normalized exponential seed, one layer per shift.
outputs.constraints: Finite and strictly positive; sum(volume * distribution) = 1 per shift.

outputs.name: thermal_speed_m_s
outputs.description: The thermal speed sqrt(2 e T_norm / (m m_H)), with m_H the hydrogen mass constant, used to convert the shifts.

outputs.name: exponent
outputs.description: The raw (unclamped) exponent per mesh node and shift.
outputs.constraints: Finite and nonpositive for accepted input; a zero entry marks a mesh node exactly at the shifted peak, where the raw seed keeps exp(0) = 1 before normalization.

preconditions: The caller supplies a consistent velocity mesh and the cylindrical cell-volume measure, in the source's N1 convention.
The caller understands the seed is the pre-compensation stage and does not treat it as a moment-compensated distribution.
supported: Per-shift Maxwellian seeds on an explicit cylindrical mesh with per-shift temperatures, for molecule_count 1 or 2.
The far-shift limit where every exponent sits below the -80 floor: the normalized seed becomes exactly the uniform distribution over the mesh.
Composition with the cylindrical velocity quadrature and with the Maxwellian relative-speed rate average on the same mesh snapshot.
excluded: Any downstream moment-compensation step: this leaf returns the seed before compensation.
Non-Maxwellian or non-exponential seeds, and any collision or field model.
Mesh or volume generation: both are caller inputs.
Unit conversion between mesh units and m/s beyond the shift division by the thermal speed.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError when vr, vx or shifted_vx_m_s is empty, when array shapes are inconsistent, when an array contains non-real, non-numeric or non-finite values, when tnorm_ev or mass_amu is not a real numeric finite positive scalar, when molecule_count is not an integer scalar equal to 1 or 2, when a temperature is nonpositive, or when a volume is nonpositive. Boolean and numeric-string arrays are not coerced.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Raises ValueError when the thermal speed, the raw exponent or the normalized distribution is not representable in double precision for finite inputs that satisfy the stated domain -- for example a normalization temperature at 1e308 whose thermal speed overflows, a tiny normalization temperature with a huge shift whose quotient overflows to an infinite exponent, a 1e-320 cell volume whose normalization denominator underflows so the divided distribution overflows to infinity, or cell volumes near the float64 ceiling whose weighted raw seed sums overflow so the divided distribution collapses to exact zeros. Every accepted call then returns finite strictly-positive distributions with a unit volume-weighted sum by construction of the clamp and the checked normalization. There is no iteration and no callback.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; no iteration. Any moment-compensation step is outside this leaf.
failure_semantics.partial_results: Never returned; a rejected call produces no outputs.

python.signature: build_shifted_maxwellian_seed(*, vr, vx, tnorm_ev, shifted_vx_m_s, temperature_ev, mass_amu, molecule_count, cylindrical_volume)

example.description: Build the seed for one shift on a small mesh, verify the volume-weighted normalization, and compose the quadrature, the seed and the Maxwellian rate average on one mesh snapshot.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.neutrals import build_shifted_maxwellian_seed, make_cylindrical_velocity_quadrature
from scirel.collisions import average_cross_section_over_maxwellian

vr = np.array([0.5, 1.5])
vx = np.array([-1.5, -0.5, 0.5, 1.5])
quadrature = make_cylindrical_velocity_quadrature(vr=vr, vx=vx)
volume = quadrature['volume']
seed = build_shifted_maxwellian_seed(
    vr=vr, vx=vx, tnorm_ev=20.0,
    shifted_vx_m_s=np.array([0.0]),
    temperature_ev=np.array([10.0]),
    mass_amu=2.0, molecule_count=1,
    cylindrical_volume=volume,
)
assert seed['distribution'].shape == (2, 4, 1)
assert np.sum(volume * seed['distribution'][:, :, 0]) == 1.0
assert np.all(np.isfinite(seed['distribution']))
rate = average_cross_section_over_maxwellian(
    particle_energy_ev=np.array([0.0, 10.0]),
    particle_mass_amu=1.0,
    target_temperature_ev=10.0,
    target_mass_amu=2.0,
    vx=vx, vr=vr, tnorm_ev=20.0,
    cylindrical_volume=volume,
    cross_section_m2=lambda energy: np.full_like(energy, 3.0e-20),
)
assert np.all(np.isfinite(rate)) and np.all(rate > 0.0)
try:
    build_shifted_maxwellian_seed(
        vr=vr, vx=vx, tnorm_ev=20.0,
        shifted_vx_m_s=np.array([0.0]),
        temperature_ev=np.array([10.0]),
        mass_amu=2.0, molecule_count=3,
        cylindrical_volume=volume,
    )
except ValueError as error:
    assert 'physical' in str(error)
else:
    raise AssertionError('molecule_count 3 must be rejected')
example.expected: The seed distribution has shape (2, 4, 1) with a volume-weighted sum of exactly 1 over the mesh, finite everywhere; the same mesh snapshot's quadrature volumes also feed the Maxwellian rate average to finite positive rates; and molecule_count 3 raises ValueError naming the physical-input contract.

scope: That the public callable reproduces the seed relation exactly: distribution, exponent and thermal speed compared against an in-file loop-per-shift formulation of the same discrete relation at rtol 1e-15.
Volume-weighted normalization: sum(volume * distribution) = 1 per shift for the supplied cell volumes.

The analytic peak witness intentionally corrects the former zero-exponent floor assertion: exp(0) = 1 before normalization. Independent Maxwell-Boltzmann peak/adjacent-node ratios exp(molecule_count) are checked at rtol 1e-15 for molecule counts 1/2, hydrogen mass multipliers 1/2 and zero/nonzero aligned drifts. A mixed peak/tail slice retains the -80 tail floor and the raw exponent output.
The far-shift limit: when every exponent sits below the -80 floor, the normalized seed is exactly the uniform distribution over the mesh.
The molecule-count factor: molecule_count 2 doubles the exponent and the distribution matches the in-file loop formulation of the same relation at molecule_count 2 with unit normalization.
A positive shift moves the volume-weighted axial moment positive.
The composition contract: the cylindrical quadrature's volumes normalize the seed and feed the Maxwellian relative-speed rate average on one immutable mesh snapshot.

Output representability: a normalization temperature at 1e308 (thermal-speed overflow), a tiny normalization temperature with a 1e308 shift (infinite raw exponent), a 1e-320 cell volume (normalization denominator underflows, divided distribution overflows) and cell volumes near the float64 ceiling (weighted raw seed sums overflow, divided distribution collapses to zeros) are each rejected with a ValueError. Inputs without a zero exponent produce unchanged numbers.

The input contract: nonempty shift layers, shape consistency, real numeric finite values, positive temperatures/masses/tnorm, integer molecule_count exactly 1 or 2, and strictly positive volumes; every out-of-domain value is rejected.

known_limitations: The seed is explicitly the pre-compensation stage: any moment-compensation step is outside this leaf, so this distribution is not the final compensated result.
The constants are fixed historical values, not current best estimates; AMU_KG names the hydrogen mass rather than standard amu, and no conversion is performed.
The exponent floor is a numerical device: distribution values in the floored region carry no exponential resolution, and the uniform-limit regime must not be read as a physical Maxwellian.
Independent analytic peak ratios are checked; no separately executed external numerical oracle is recorded, and the retained tail floor remains an approximation.
The contract does not establish: Any downstream moment-compensation step: this leaf returns the seed before compensation..

The exponent oracle and the covariance identity are exact for the discrete relation; the tail floor itself remains a numerical device, so the floored region carries no analytic exponential value and the uniform far-shift limit is not a physical Maxwellian.
